_source: CORE ELA Pacing Guide 6th Grade - Open Up EL Education, uploaded 8/31/26, transcribed by week (parsed from the guide's M | U | L labels and lesson titles, cross-checked against Appendix A's Grade 6 ELA bullets in 2627_LP_Meeting_Plan.md).
_note: Module = EL Education Module, Unit = the Unit within that Module (stored as a string; lesson numbers reset per Unit, as in Grades K-5). Five weeks cross a Unit boundary within the same Module - week 4 (Unit 1 to Unit 2), week 7 (Unit 2 to Unit 3), week 13 (Unit 1 to Unit 2), week 29 (Unit 1 to Unit 2), and week 33 (Unit 2 to Unit 3) - each split into two segments per the standing rule; every Module-to-Module transition (weeks 10, 19, 28) lands cleanly on a week boundary with no crossing. This guide runs the full 36 weeks with no early finish, matching Grades 4 and 5. New at this grade: many lessons carry a duplicate '(Homework)' or '*Complete over 2 days' entry under the same lesson number (e.g. week 2's L7 and L7 (Homework), week 26's L8 printed twice for a two-day lesson). These are the same lesson, not new content, and are deduped to a single lesson number rather than double-counted - confirmed this never breaks contiguity, since every Module/Unit pair still runs 1..N with no gaps. 'assessment' names any Mid-Unit / End-of-Unit Assessment or Performance Task falling within that segment's lessons - 'Mid-Unit'/'End of Unit'/'Part I/II' and colon detail are dropped, keeping only the base tag; a tag repeated across lessons in the same segment, or across two consecutive weeks for a multi-day assessment (e.g. weeks 6-7's End of Unit 2 Assessment, weeks 26-27's Mid-to-End Unit 3 Assessment sequence, week 36's Part I/II End of Unit 3 Assessment), is written once per segment. No guide header typos found in this guide (unlike prior grades' M|U|L mislabels) - every lesson's stated M|U|L matches its title and its place in the week's own sequence. Confirmed against Appendix A's Grade 6 Open Up EL Education bullets in 2627_LP_Meeting_Plan.md, which for this grade already carry the same per-week breakdown as the guide itself (unlike the compressed one-line-per-LP ranges at other grades) - every closed range agrees exactly across all 10 LPs, zero boundary mismatches, cleaner than Grade 5 ELA's two typo-driven differences and matching this same grade's Math file. Lesson accounting is contiguous from 1 with no gaps or duplicates across all twelve Module/Unit pairs (M1: 16, 14, 12 lessons; M2: 15, 12, 15; M3: 15, 13, 13; M4: 8, 16, 17), 166 lessons total.
